acts.desc: When it comes to disciplining young people, teachers are winging it. We ask middle school teachers all over the country to walk us through how they get a kid to take his hat off. The book Ira mentions is called Building a Better Teacher by reporter Elizabeth Green; it’s eye-opening in a number of ways. (5 1/2 minutes)
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: We start out exploration of discipline and schools at the very beginning … in preschool. Tunette Powell is a writer in Omaha and mother to JJ and Joah.
acts.title: Time Out

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
About 20 years ago, a group of educators launched one of the biggest recent experiments in
American education when they started creating charter schools designed for poor, minority kids.
The idea was to create classrooms that are rigorous and strict. We talk with a student named
Rousseau Mieze, who grew up in a school like that and then became a teacher.
acts.title: The Guinea Pig Becomes the Scientist

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: We spend a semester in a public school in New York City called Lyons Community School. Lyons is trying to avoid suspensions, detentions and basically all other forms of traditional punishment.
acts.title: The Talking Cure
